transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Please, come in, Mr. Okonkwo. Thank you for coming back to see us today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to start by being very direct with you. During your surgery, a mistake was made. A surgical clip was placed on the wrong structure inside your abdomen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The wrong structure? What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means we clamped a piece of tissue that should not have been clamped. I am deeply sorry. This was our error, and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was told everything went well when I woke up. Now you are telling me this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to process and it is a difficult thing to hear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have a position in my community. People look to me. If it comes out that my surgery was botched, it makes me look weak, or like I cannot manage my own affairs. My children... they worry enough as it is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you are feeling a great deal of pressure to maintain your dignity and your standing in the family, and this news feels like a threat to that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is. It is an embarrassment. To be put under a knife and then to be told it wasn't done right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I can only imagine how unsettling it is to feel that your trust was misplaced.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, what happened? You said a clip. What exactly did you do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We use these small metal clips to seal off vessels. In this case, the clip was placed on a nearby structure instead of the target vessel. We call this a misplaced clip. Because it was in the wrong spot, we had to perform an additional procedure right there in the operating room to remove it and fix the area before we closed you up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And this additional procedure... did it cause more damage?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It required more time under anesthesia and a slightly larger manipulation of the tissue, but we corrected it before you left the table.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you are sure it is fixed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, we verified the correction before finishing the surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I do not know how I am supposed to tell my wife. She thinks I am recovered.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a heavy burden to carry. Please take all the time you need. I am here with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need more surgery now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, the correction was made during the first operation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then why am I here today?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Because it is my duty to tell you exactly what happened, even if the immediate physical problem was solved. You deserved to know that a mistake occurred.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate you telling me. I suppose I would be more angry if I found out from someone else. But I still feel... shaken.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a completely natural way to feel. You trusted us with your body, and we failed to meet the standard of care you deserved. I am truly sorry for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? How do we make sure this doesn't happen again to someone else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Looking into it how?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, we'll probably have a meeting about it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan, Doctor. Who is checking my recovery now? Do I need more scans?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Keep an eye on things? I need to know if I should be looking for specific symptoms. Is there a follow-up appointment?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can probably just schedule something later on.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Later on when? Next month? Next year?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure of the schedule right now. I'll have my team look into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I came here for answers, but now I feel like I am drifting.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. I really do. I know this feels uncertain.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is uncertain. I am a leader in my community, and I cannot lead if I am wondering if my insides are actually healed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that the uncertainty is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a date. A specific date for a check-up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see what I can do. I think we'll just reach out via email or a call.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not want an email. I want a plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will get it sorted.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to speak fully without interruption and remains regulated and calm despite the patient's increasing frustration.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and lay language was used, but there were no comprehension checks performed to ensure the patient understood the explanation.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am deeply sorry'), takes full responsibility, and maintains this accountability throughout the encounter.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('pressure to maintain your dignity', 'unsettling', 'frustrating') and references the patient's specific concerns about his community standing.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague responses ('we'll probably have a meeting', 'keep an eye on things', 'get it sorted') without specific dates or a concrete plan.
